nodes.title: matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)') returns false while other WCO signals report active
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.3.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Reproduced on Nobara 43 (Fedora-based, KDE Plasma 6, kernel 6.19.10) under both X11 and Wayland sessions, and on Windows 11 (23H2) in a VM today.

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

None within the currently-supported window. The same probe reproduces identically on 38.8.6 (Chromium 140), 39.8.9 (Chromium 142), 40.9.2 (Chromium 144), and 41.3.0 (Chromium 146) on Linux, and on 41.3.0 on Windows 11. Either this has always been wrong or it regressed before 38, which is EOL.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When a `BrowserWindow` is created with `frame: false`, `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'`, and a populated `titleBarOverlay` object, all four standard WCO entry points should agree:

1. `navigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible` → `true`
2. `windowControlsOverlay.getTitlebarAreaRect()` → non-zero rect
3. `env(titlebar-area-width / -height / -x / -y)` → populated CSS env values
4. `matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)').matches` → `true`

The W3C [Window Controls Overlay explainer](https://github.com/WICG/window-controls-overlay/blob/main/explainer.md) and the [MDN docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window_Controls_Overlay_API) both name the media query as the recommended CSS detection point.

### Actual Behavior

Three of four signals report WCO active. **Only `matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)')` disagrees and returns `matches: false`.** The same mismatch reproduces on Linux and on Windows 11.

Probe output, Electron 41.3.0, Linux (Wayland; X11 identical):

```
navigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible                       : true
getTitlebarAreaRect() width × height                          : 804 × 40
env(titlebar-area-width)                                      : 804px
env(titlebar-area-height)                                     : 40px
matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)').matches : false
```

Probe output, Electron 41.3.0, Windows 11:

```
navigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible                       : true
getTitlebarAreaRect() width × height                          : 763 × 40
env(titlebar-area-width)                                      : 763px
env(titlebar-area-height)                                     : 40px
matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)').matches : false
```

The titlebar-area rect matches the configured `titleBarOverlay.height: 40` on both platforms, which confirms Chromium has applied WCO at the layout level. The CSS `env()` values share that source. But pages following the W3C-recommended detection pattern see WCO as inactive and skip the WCO-specific layout they would have rendered.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/aaddrick/90a16bf22da070e07ff382c7a89ae3d8

### Additional Information

**Relationship to #51389.** I filed [#51389](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/51389) earlier today framing this as Linux-specific. After source investigation and a Windows 11 reproduction, that framing was wrong. I withdrew #51389 and am refiling here with the corrected scope. The probe output, gist, and sibling repo are unchanged; only the platform list and the root-cause section are new.

**Root cause.** Electron's `WebContents` (`shell/browser/api/electron_api_web_contents.h:124-125`) inherits from `content::WebContentsDelegate` and overrides ~50 methods. It does not override `GetDisplayMode()`. A full grep of the tree confirms zero references to `display_mode` outside two unrelated header includes. Without an override, Chromium's default returns `blink::mojom::DisplayMode::kBrowser`, which gets baked into `WebPreferences::display_mode` in `RenderViewHostImpl::ComputeWebPreferences()` and shipped to Blink. The matchMedia evaluator for `(display-mode: …)` reads from there, so it always evaluates against `kBrowser` regardless of how the BrowserWindow was configured.

The other three signals work because they take a separate mojo path: `NativeWindow::NotifyLayoutWindowControlsOverlay()` → `BrowserWindow::UpdateWindowControlsOverlay()` (`electron_api_browser_window.cc:205`) → `web_contents()->UpdateWindowControlsOverlay(rect)`. That path never touches the `display_mode` web preference, so it stays at `kBrowser` and the four signals diverge.

**Fix.** I have a 16-line patch on a local branch that overrides `GetDisplayMode()` on Electron's `WebContents` and routes the answer through the same `IsWindowControlsOverlayEnabled()` gate (`native_window.h:390-398`) the other three signals already use. Same input, same answer; the four signals agree by construction. The override also returns `kFullscreen` for fullscreen windows and `kStandalone` for frameless windows without titleBarOverlay, which matches Chromium's PWA semantics so existing `isStandalone()`-style checks (e.g., the one in microsoft/vscode#160696) keep working. With the patch applied on Linux, the probe table reads `matches: true` and all four signals agree. PR coming separately.

**Sibling repo with the Chromium PWA companion test.** I published the same Electron Fiddle files alongside a Chromium-side PWA repro at https://github.com/aaddrick/wco-matchMedia-mismatch. The Electron repro lives at the repo root (mirrors the gist). The Chromium-side test is under [`chromium-pwa/`](https://github.com/aaddrick/wco-matchMedia-mismatch/tree/master/chromium-pwa). Either source works.

**AI disclosure** (per the Electron governance AI policy): I drafted the repro and this report with assistance from Anthropic's Opus 4.7 via Claude Code. I ran the repro locally on Electron 41.3.0 (Nobara 43 / KDE Plasma 6 / Wayland) and on a Windows 11 VM, empirically verified the four-signal mismatch on both, and reviewed this body line-by-line before submission. I'm responsible for the contents and can answer follow-up questions.

**How I ran into this.** It surfaced during [aaddrick/claude-desktop-debian#538](https://github.com/aaddrick/claude-desktop-debian/pull/538), packaging an Electron-based web app for Linux. The bundled web app uses `matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)')` to decide whether to render its WCO-aware topbar. On Electron Linux that returns `false` even though WCO is active, so the topbar silently doesn't render. I assumed it was Linux-only because that's where I first saw it; the Windows VM repro disproved that.

**Concrete impact.** Pages whose conditional WCO layout relies on the `@media (display-mode: window-controls-overlay)` rule render their non-WCO layout while WCO is active, which causes visual collisions with the overlay area on every Electron platform. Pages that detect via `navigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible` work correctly. Most JS-side detection examples in the wild use one or both, and any that use only the `@media` route are silently broken.

nodes.title: Linux: matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)') returns false while other WCO signals report active
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.3.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Nobara 43 (Fedora-based), KDE Plasma 6, kernel 6.19.10. I reproduced it under both X11 and Wayland sessions.

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

None within the currently-supported window. I tested the same repro against Electron 38.8.6 (Chromium 140), 39.8.9 (Chromium 142), 40.9.2 (Chromium 144), and 41.3.0 (Chromium 146); the matchMedia mismatch reproduces identically on every one of them, with the other three signals reporting WCO active and the same `804 × 40` rect each time. So this isn't a regression within the supported window. Either the bridge has always been wrong on Linux or it regressed before Electron 38, which is already EOL.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

When a `BrowserWindow` is created with `frame: false`, `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'`, and a populated `titleBarOverlay` object, all four standard Window-Controls-Overlay entry points should agree that WCO is active:

1. `navigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible` → `true`
2. `windowControlsOverlay.getTitlebarAreaRect()` → non-zero rect
3. `env(titlebar-area-width / -height / -x / -y)` → populated CSS env values
4. `matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)').matches` → `true`

That's the agreement pages rely on for WCO-aware layout. The [Window Controls Overlay explainer](https://github.com/WICG/window-controls-overlay/blob/main/explainer.md) and the [MDN docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window_Controls_Overlay_API) both document the media query as the recommended CSS detection point.

### Actual Behavior

Three of the four signals correctly report WCO is active. **Only the `matchMedia` query disagrees and returns `matches: false`.**

Probe output from the attached repro running on Electron 41.3.0 (Wayland session, but X11 produces the same result; identical output verified on 38.8.6, 39.8.9, 40.9.2 — see *Last Known Working Electron version* above):

```
navigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible                       : true
getTitlebarAreaRect() width × height                          : 804 × 40
env(titlebar-area-width)                                      : 804px
env(titlebar-area-height)                                     : 40px
matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)').matches : false
```

The titlebar-area rect (804 × 40) matches the configured `titleBarOverlay.height: 40`, which confirms Chromium has applied WCO at the layout level. The CSS `env()` values come from the same source. But pages following the W3C-recommended detection pattern (`matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)')` and the corresponding `@media` rule) see WCO as inactive and skip whatever WCO-specific layout they would have rendered.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/aaddrick/90a16bf22da070e07ff382c7a89ae3d8

### Additional Information

**Issue tracker searches** (extending the Preflight checkbox above). I searched for `windowControlsOverlay`, `WCO`, `titleBarOverlay`, `display-mode window-controls-overlay`, and `matchMedia display-mode`. No existing match. The closest neighbors are #34947 (BrowserView WCO support, separate concern) and #51000 / #45798 (Linux WCO button order / native context menu, different surfaces).

**Sibling repo with the Chromium PWA companion test.** I also published the same Electron Fiddle files alongside a Chromium-side PWA repro at https://github.com/aaddrick/wco-matchMedia-mismatch. The Electron repro lives at the repo root (it mirrors the gist linked above), and the Chromium-side test is under [`chromium-pwa/`](https://github.com/aaddrick/wco-matchMedia-mismatch/tree/master/chromium-pwa). Either source works. I included the gist to satisfy the standard testcase-gist convention, and the repo carries the additional Chromium investigation that doesn't fit a flat gist.

**AI disclosure** (per the Electron governance AI policy): I drafted the repro and this report with assistance from Anthropic's Opus 4.7 via Claude Code. I then ran the repro locally on Electron 41.3.0 (Nobara 43 / KDE Plasma 6 / Wayland), empirically verified the four-signal mismatch, and reviewed this body line-by-line before submission. I'm responsible for the contents and can answer follow-up questions.

**Chromium activation paths I tried on Linux.** I tried three separate paths to reproduce against Google Chrome 147.0.7727.55 on the same Linux box. None of them activate the WCO API surface in plain Chromium on Linux:

1. **Install as a PWA.** I packaged an equivalent app (manifest with `"display_override": ["window-controls-overlay"]`, served over `http://localhost`, installed via the omnibox install icon). Chrome parses the manifest and the registrar resolves the display mode to `window-controls-overlay`, but the per-app boolean `window_controls_overlay_enabled` stays `false` and there's no UI control to flip it on Linux. From `chrome://web-app-internals` for the installed app:

   ```
   "display_override": ["window-controls-overlay"],
   "registrar_evaluated_fields": { "display_mode": "window-controls-overlay", … },
   "window_controls_overlay_enabled": false,
   "user_display_mode": "kStandalone"
   ```

   The PWA opens in `display: standalone`. All four signals report inactive.

2. **`chrome://flags`.** The historical `enable-desktop-pwas-window-controls-overlay` flag from the original [Intent to Experiment](https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/blink-dev/c/HNHbpxvrECA) isn't in Chrome 147 anymore. The feature shipped stable in Chrome 102 and the flag was retired. Adjacent flags (`enable-desktop-pwas-borderless`, `enable-desktop-pwas-additional-windowing-controls`, `enable-desktop-pwas-tab-strip*`) are unrelated to WCO activation.

3. **DevTools Application → Manifest → "Emulate the Window Controls Overlay".** The checkbox draws OS-style window-control buttons over the page area, but it doesn't plumb any of the four API signals. `navigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible` stays `false`, `getTitlebarAreaRect()` returns `0×0`, `env(titlebar-area-*)` is empty, and `matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)')` returns `false`. The emulation is visual-only on Linux Chrome 147. This contradicts [devtoolstips.org's description of the feature](https://devtoolstips.org/tips/en/simulate-pwa-wco/), which says the env values should activate. In my test on Linux they did not.

So there's no path to observe Chromium-side WCO API behaviour on Linux today, and therefore no upstream baseline I could produce locally. There is, however, prior-art evidence that upstream Chromium handles this correctly elsewhere: [microsoft/vscode#160696](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/160696) explicitly documents that Chromium *does* match `(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)` from `matchMedia` when WCO is active for installed PWAs. That places the divergence on Electron's `titleBarOverlay` activation path, not on upstream Blink — Electron's path activates the visible / rect / env signals on Linux (as shown in *Actual Behavior* above) but the `matchMedia` evaluator stays detached from that activation. If a maintainer knows of a way to force `window_controls_overlay_enabled: true` on Linux Chrome (a custom build, a LevelDB patch, a CDP method I missed), I'm happy to re-test. The Chromium PWA repro itself lives at [`chromium-pwa/`](https://github.com/aaddrick/wco-matchMedia-mismatch/tree/master/chromium-pwa) in the sibling repo linked above.

**How I ran into this.** It surfaced during [aaddrick/claude-desktop-debian#538](https://github.com/aaddrick/claude-desktop-debian/pull/538). I was packaging an Electron-based web app for Linux and trying to match the Windows / macOS topbar layout. The bundled web app uses `matchMedia('(display-mode: window-controls-overlay)')` to decide whether to render its WCO-aware topbar. On Electron Linux that returns `false` even though WCO is active, so the topbar silently doesn't render and the Linux build can't match the Windows layout despite the BrowserWindow being configured identically. Side-by-side, with the same app and identical `titleBarOverlay` config:

Windows:

![Windows: single-bar topbar with hamburger / sidebar / search / back-forward / ghost icons inline with the window controls](https://github.com/aaddrick/wco-matchMedia-mismatch/raw/master/docs/screenshots/windows-titlebar.png)

Linux (best achievable with the current workaround):

![Linux: stacked layout — DE-drawn titlebar on top, in-app topbar below, no inline window controls](https://github.com/aaddrick/wco-matchMedia-mismatch/raw/master/docs/screenshots/linux-titlebar.png)

The full investigation chain, including two adjacent Linux WCO observations that turned out to already be tracked at #34947 and #37789, is in [`docs/learnings/linux-topbar-shim.md`](https://github.com/aaddrick/claude-desktop-debian/blob/experiment/linux-topbar-wco/docs/learnings/linux-topbar-shim.md). Our current workaround is a preload shim that overrides `matchMedia` (and a couple of adjacent surfaces). A fix here would let us drop the `matchMedia` portion of that shim.

**Why I think it's worth filing despite Linux WCO being a moving target.** The mismatch is internal to Electron's own WCO surface. Three of four entry points agree the feature is active; only the documented detection point disagrees. That contradiction is independent of whether WCO behaves correctly elsewhere on Linux, and it silently breaks any web app that does feature detection the W3C-recommended way (`matchMedia` / `@media (display-mode: window-controls-overlay)`). The activation-paths investigation above also implies this is reachable only via Electron on Linux today, since plain Chromium-Linux doesn't expose a path to activate WCO for installed PWAs.

**Concrete impact.** Pages whose conditional WCO layout relies on the `@media` rule render their non-WCO layout while WCO is active, which leads to visual collisions with the overlay area. Pages that detect via `navigator.windowControlsOverlay.visible` work correctly. Most JS-side detection examples in the wild use one or both, and any that use only the `@media` route are silently broken on Electron Linux today.

nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.3.0 (also reproducible on 36.9.5)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.4.1 (25E253) — also reported on 26.3.1 (25D2128)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

None confirmed. The shipping build that crashes was Electron 36.9.5; bumping to 41.3.0 produces a similar crash with slightly different V8 frames, suggesting the bug spans the 36 → 41 range under macOS 26 + MAS sandbox.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

A correctly-signed, MAS-sandboxed Electron app should launch normally on macOS 26.x when delivered through TestFlight or the Mac App Store.

### Actual Behavior

App crashes at startup with `EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)` / `brk 0` on a thread named `ThreadPoolSingleThreadForegroundBlocking0`. Crash occurs ~2 seconds after launch on Electron 36, ~13 seconds on Electron 41 — gets further in initialization on the newer version but dies in the same place. No window is ever shown.

The crash signature has two consistent characteristics:

I do not have a public minimal repro yet, but the failure conditions are tightly specified:

1. Electron app distributed via Mac App Store (MAS sandbox enabled).
2. Hardened runtime enabled (`CS_RUNTIME` set on every Mach-O — verified via `codesign -dvv` showing `flags=0x10000(runtime)` on main + helpers).
3. Entitlements include `com.apple.security.app-sandbox`, `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit` (with or without `cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory` — tested both, no difference).
4. Running on macOS 26.x (confirmed on 26.3.1 and 26.4.1).
5. Apple Silicon (arm64).
6. Delivered through the App Store / TestFlight channel (so the bundle has a valid `_MASReceipt`; sideloaded MAS-signed bundles do not launch on modern macOS regardless of correctness — that's a separate AMFI gate, not this bug).

I'm happy to build a minimal Electron-Forge / electron-quick-start MAS-signed sample and upload it via TestFlight if that would help. Please let me know what would be most useful.

These are documented to save the next person's time:

1. **Bumped Electron 36.9.5 → 41.3.0.** Crash signature changed slightly (V8 was rewritten) but failure mode identical.
2. **Re-signed with Apple's `codesign` instead of `rcodesign`.** Signing pipeline became cleaner but the runtime crash was unaffected — both signers were producing valid signatures all along.
3. **Added `app.commandLine.appendSwitch('no-proxy-server')` to the main process** before `app.whenReady()`. Hypothesis: Chromium's PAC V8 isolate on a worker thread was the crash site. Crash unchanged.
4. **Removed `com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory`** from entitlements (it's deprecated on macOS 14+ and theoretically conflicts with `cs.allow-jit`). Crash unchanged.
5. **Verified TestFlight delivery channel.** App was installed via TestFlight (visible in crash reports as `Beta: YES`, `is_beta: 1`, `entitledBeta: true`), confirming we're past every signing/profile/entitlement validation gate. The crash is purely runtime.

## Hypothesis

V8's JIT-page handling on worker threads (specifically the `ThreadPoolSingleThreadForegroundBlocking0` thread that handles DNS / network-resolver work in Chromium) is hitting a MAP_JIT lifecycle issue on macOS 26 under the MAS sandbox. macOS 26 tightened MAP_JIT enforcement: pages need explicit `pthread_jit_write_protect_np()` toggles, and worker threads in Chromium's network/resolver subsystem appear to lose RX permission before V8 attempts to execute. Under hardened runtime + sandbox, the resulting fault is fatal.

The pattern of "DNS-blocking thread + V8 frames + parallel worker hitting Instruction Abort with `pc == far`" is consistent across both Electron 36 and 41, which is why I think this is at the V8/Chromium layer rather than something specific to either Electron release.

- Build pipeline: `electron-builder` (no signing) → custom shell script using Apple's `codesign` (inside-out: dylibs/.node files → frameworks → helpers → main bundle) → `productbuild`.
- Signing identity: `3rd Party Mac Developer Application: Anish Varghese (65UF42MSBU)`.
- Provisioning profile: STORE distribution, valid until 2027.
- Hardened runtime: enabled on every Mach-O (`flags=0x10000(runtime)`).
- DER entitlements: present (verified via `codesign -d --entitlements -`).
- Native modules in bundle: `node-llama-cpp` and `nodejs-whisper` (both inert at runtime under MAS via `process.mas` guards), `@reflink/reflink-darwin-arm64` (active).

## Additional Information

The same app:
- Runs fine in `npm run dev` (unsandboxed Electron 41.3.0) on the same macOS 26.4.1 machine.
- Runs fine on macOS 15.x with the MAS-signed build.
- Is currently shipping on the App Store at version 1.3.1 (build 7, Electron 36.9.5) and crashing for all macOS 26 users.

nodes.title: [Feature Request]: Support per-corner radii in View.setBorderRadius()
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

## Problem Description

`View.setBorderRadius(radius)` currently only accepts a single uniform radius.

I am building a browser-like UI in Electron with:

- a custom top navigation / toolbar area
- a webpage content area below it
- a composed surface that should look like a single rounded browser container

In this kind of layout, I often need different radii per corner instead of one radius for all four corners.

A common example is:

- top toolbar: rounded top-left / top-right corners, square bottom corners
- content area: square top corners, rounded bottom-left / bottom-right corners

With the current API, a uniform radius is not expressive enough for this kind of browser-style composition.

This is especially relevant when using `WebContentsView` for the page content and native `View`s for the surrounding shell UI. I can build the layout, but I cannot describe the corner geometry precisely enough with the current API shape.


### Proposed Solution

Extend `View.setBorderRadius()` to support per-corner radii in addition to the existing single-number form.

For example:

```js
view.setBorderRadius(12)

view.setBorderRadius({
  topLeft: 12,
  topRight: 12,
  bottomRight: 0,
  bottomLeft: 0
})
```

This would preserve backward compatibility while allowing browser-like shells and other composed native layouts to be expressed much more cleanly.

A per-corner object form also feels less error-prone and more self-documenting than a positional multi-argument overload.

## Why This Would Help

My use case is to simulate a browser interface where the custom top navigation bar and the webpage content area visually belong to the same rounded container.

Today, the lack of per-corner control makes this difficult:

- a single radius rounds corners that should remain square
- splitting the UI across multiple native views becomes visually awkward
- browser-like composition requires extra workarounds for something that is fundamentally a corner-geometry problem



### Alternatives Considered

- Applying CSS `border-radius` / `clip-path` inside the webpage.
  This is not a reliable substitute when the content is arbitrary web content, because page-controlled root backgrounds, loading skeletons, or transitions can make the result fragile.

- Building a more complex native wrapper around the content.
  This is possible, but it is a much heavier solution than simply allowing per-corner radii on the existing API.


### Additional Information

I am not asking this API to change the current clipping or hit-testing model of `setBorderRadius()`.

This request is specifically about allowing asymmetric / per-corner radii so Electron apps can build browser-like native layouts more precisely.

I wrote it to push the strongest argument for your real use case. If you want, I can also rewrite this into a version that explicitly asks for the 4-argument signature `setBorderRadius(topLeft, topRight, bottomRight, bottomLeft)`.

nodes.title: [Documentation]: Emphasise platform differences still exist with cross-platform support
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Referring to Electron as cross-platform may cause developers to overlook how, even though one JavaScript codebase works for Windows, macOS, and Linux, performance characteristics aren't always the same for all platforms.

I filed an issue to address this for one case earlier:
- https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/49727

There, the issue was the `app.getApplicationNameForProtocol` API performing much worse on Linux, as compared to Windows and macOS. The performance disparity was caught as I was testing the application on Linux, in addition to the main developer testing on macOS and Windows.

While the API documentation states **platform availability**, such as an API only being available on macOS, it generally doesn't include whether **performance** might differ across platforms that are supported.

I believe this could mislead developers into thinking an Electron application performs the same across all platforms, and, as a result, overlook any platform specific issues that may come up.

### Proposed Solution

Add a section in [`Docs > Best Practices > Performance`](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/performance) that emphasises the possibility for issues to only exist on one platform, even though Electron is a cross-platform framework.

I was thinking a section like:
> ## Platform Differences
> While Electron is a cross-platform framework, there may still be differences between platforms. An API, although it may support Windows, macOS, and Linux, is not guaranteed to **perform** the same across them.
>
> During development, be aware of the possibility that the performance of an Electron application running on your local device may not necessarily be identical performance-wise to the same application running on another platform. 

### Alternatives Considered

These performance differences could also be documented for each API.

I imagine this idea wouldn't be mutually exclusive with the first one.

### Additional Information

I'm making this issue primarily to get any others' thoughts on this, as I reckon this is a pretty big topic.

Happy to have a discussion 🙂

nodes.title: Add API to get cursor position relative to the window
nodes.body:

- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

It's possible to get the position of the mouse cursor relative to the display with `screen.getCursorPoint()`.

On Wayland, this function inadvertently gave the cursor position relative to the active _window_ rather than the display. While this was not the intended behaviour, it is still a useful capability which Electron should support for all platforms.

### Proposed Solution

Add a `BaseWindow.getCursorPoint()` API which provides coordinates relative to the window. (So 0,0 is the top left corner of the window.)

### Alternatives Considered

Developers can get the cursor position relative to web content with a DOM event listener in the renderer, e.g. `mousemove` event. However this does not work well if you use multiple web content views, and of course it does not work outside the web content area for framed windows.

### Additional Information

Refs https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/51153.

### Expected Behavior

On a frameless BrowserWindow, calling setResizable(false) should not change the values returned by getBounds() / getContentBounds(). The window's logical rect should remain equal to the rect passed to setBounds().

### Actual Behavior

After setResizable(true → false) on a frameless window, getBounds() and getContentBounds() both report a rect inflated by the resize-hit insets introduced in #50863:
- x: -8
- width: +16 (8 left + 8 right)
- height: +9 (0 top + 9 bottom)

| --- | --- | --- |
| 41.2.0 | `{x:0,y:0,w:0,h:1}` | `{x:0,y:0,w:0,h:1}` ✅ |
| 41.2.1 | `{x:0,y:0,w:0,h:1}` | `{x:-8,y:0,w:16,h:9}` ❌ |
| 41.2.2 | `{x:0,y:0,w:0,h:1}` | `{x:-8,y:0,w:16,h:9}` ❌ |
| 43.0.0-nightly.20260421 | `{x:0,y:0,w:0,h:1}` | `{x:-8,y:0,w:16,h:9}` ❌ |

The only change between 41.2.0 and 41.2.1 that touches this path is #50863.

```text

  requested  : {"x":200,"y":200,"width":400,"height":300}
  getBounds  : {"x":200,"y":200,"width":400,"height":301}
  delta      : {"x":0,"y":0,"w":0,"h":1}         <-- DPR rounding only

t2 - IMMEDIATELY after setResizable(false)

  getContent : {"x":192,"y":200,"width":416,"height":309}

```
